html:
Reza Shah was the ruler of Iran from 1925 to 1941 and founder of the Pahlavi dynasty. An officer of the Cossack Brigade, he took power in a coup in 1921 and replaced the last Qajar shah in 1925.

Like Atatürk in Turkey, he set out to make Iran modern and strong by force. He built a national army, roads and the Trans-Iranian Railway, opened Tehran University, and brought in state schools and courts that cut the power of the clergy. In 1935 he asked foreign states to call the country Iran, not Persia. In 1936 he banned women from wearing the veil in public.

In 1941 Britain and the Soviet Union invaded Iran to secure its oil and a supply route. They forced him to abdicate for his son, Mohammad Reza, and he died in exile in Johannesburg. See also Iran and Anglo-Persian Oil Company.
